comment: Every external thing a check group needs, declared once.
Before this file the knowledge was scattered across the scripts that happened
to need it: _provider_environment.sh knew two tool homes, bootstrap_kani.sh knew
the solver directory, check_formal.sh knew the pinned solver version, pg_tests.sh
knew two container images, doctor.sh kept a prose table that nothing compared
against reality. The cost was always the same shape: an absent tool was reported
as whatever its absence happened to break -- a proof failure, a broken import, a
pull-access error -- and the symptom named the wrong cause.
scripts/ci/gate_tools.py is the only reader. doctor.sh reports from it, the gate
runners precheck from it, and its --self-test proves every row can be located by
the method it states or is legitimately absent on this machine.
locate kinds:
path           - a binary found by name on PATH
bundle         - a binary found on PATH or inside one of `directories`,
which scripts/ci/_provider_environment.sh appends to PATH
kani-bundle    - a binary inside `scripts/ci/bootstrap_kani.sh --solver-tools`
cargo-bin      - a cargo subcommand, i.e. a `cargo-<name>` binary on PATH
rust-toolchain - a named toolchain listed by `rustup toolchain list`
file           - a file at `path`, overridable by `env_override`
container-image- an image an engine must be able to run
node-root      - a package root whose node_modules a gate imports;
check_node_dependencies.py owns the decision
builtin        - compiled into another tool, so there is nothing to locate
requirement: `required` means the gate cannot run without it and the runner must
fail by name; `optional` means the gate skips a named part of its work and `skip`
says which part; `fetched` means the engine downloads it at first use, so a
locally absent one is reported with its pull command rather than failed.

disk_minimums.reason: CBMC writes whole-program GOTO binaries per harness. A short write truncates one, and the backend aborts with SIGABRT instead of reporting os error 28.
A full workspace build plus every test binary and the nextest archive.
Container image layers for the database and the object store, plus their volumes.

comment: Reclaimable build space, and the rules that make reclaiming it safe.
scripts/ci/reclaim_build_space.py is the only reader; docs/adr/0080 states the policy.
The machine filled up twice in one session. 152 of 219 checkouts carried an
in-tree target/ totalling 509G against ~1.1G of source each, the shared cargo
intermediates had grown to 1.4T, and a stale /data tree held another 129G.
A full filesystem does not announce itself: it reached CBMC as os error 28,
truncated a GOTO binary, and crashed the backend with SIGABRT.
Build output is derived. A checkout, its history and its uncommitted changes
are not, and nothing here may touch them.
safety_rules: Only a build-output directory is ever removed: an in-tree `target/` of a git checkout, a cargo target directory directly under a declared target root, or one entry of a shared cargo-intermediates root.
A checkout, a `.git` directory or file, a bare repository and any source tree are never touched, whatever their age.

A path is in use when a live process has its cwd at or inside it, or names it in CARGO_TARGET_DIR or CARGO_BUILD_BUILD_DIR. In-use paths are kept regardless of age. Liveness is read from /proc/<pid>/cwd and /proc/<pid>/environ, never from a process-name pattern.
A path outside every declared root is never a candidate, so a typo cannot widen the scope.
Age is the newest modification time within the first two levels of the directory, so an active build is young even when its root directory is not.
needs_a_decision_instead: A worktree holding unmerged commits or uncommitted changes: its build output is still reclaimable, but the checkout itself is a person's decision, not this tool's.
The sccache disk cache: it is already capped by cache.disk size in ~/.config/sccache/config, so it is bounded rather than leaking. Report its size, do not reclaim it.

cleanup_suggestions: $CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug/incremental - rebuilt on demand, always safe to delete
target/test-timings - gate telemetry only; check-all.sh recreates it
target/formal-artifacts - previous formal diagnostics; a new run writes its own
docker image prune -f and docker container prune -f - reclaims stopped gate substrates
scripts/ci/reclaim_build_space.py - reports and reclaims idle build output across every checkout

tools.name: docker.io/library/rust:1.96-bookworm@sha256:a339861ae23e9abb272cea45dfafde21760d2ce6577a70f8a926153677902663
tools.note: rust toolchain stage of deploy/images/sandbox/Dockerfile. Required rather than fetched on demand: the gate builds from all five at once, and when the registry is slow or unreachable the on-demand path burns minutes inside buildkit and then reports `DeadlineExceeded: failed to resolve source metadata`, which reads as a broken build rather than a missing image. Deciding it in the preflight costs one lookup and names the exact pull to run. The digest is the one pinned in the Dockerfile; both must move together.
